answer.label: Traditionally attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Tradition assigns this apology to Marie Antoinette after she stepped on her executioner’s foot. The anecdote is repeated by modern sources, but a contemporary witness and the exact English wording remain unconfirmed.

source.heading: The source

author.name: Marie Antoinette
author.heading: About Marie Antoinette
author.bio: Marie Antoinette was the Austrian-born wife of Louis XVI and queen of France before the Revolution abolished the monarchy. Imprisoned with the royal family, she was tried and executed in Paris in October 1793. The story of her courtesy to the executioner belongs to the later accounts of that execution.

copyAttribution: Traditionally attributed to Marie Antoinette at her execution (16 October 1793); contemporary witness and exact English translation unconfirmed.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The story places a small act of politeness at the moment of a public execution. AFP’s conditional wording preserves an important distinction: a frequently retold incident is not the same as an authenticated transcript, and the familiar English sentence has an unidentified translator.
